title: The Higgs-top-$Z$ mass coincidence relation after NNLO matching
summary: The relation $M_H^2\simeq M_ZM_t$, previously proposed as a non-trivial Higgs mass coincidence, is reconsidered with present electroweak inputs and with a scheme-consistent matching analysis. With the 2025 PDG values for $M_Z$, $M_W$ and $M_H$, and the ATLAS-CMS direct top-mass combination, the pole-level ratio is $ρ_{Zt}=M_ZM_t/M_H^2=1.00362\pm0.00261$. Thus an exact pole-level geometric relation predicts either $M_H=125.426\pm0.120\,\mathrm{GeV}$ or $M_t=171.898\pm0.302\,\mathrm{GeV}$, which is still a $1.4σ$ test rather than an exclusion.
